answer: An economy of AI agents can achieve robust Sybil resistance by anchoring identity generation to a cryptographic vault requiring verifiable computational work or staked economic capital. When an agent node joins the network, it must register its parameters within a distributed atlas, ensuring global state consistency. If a malicious actor attempts to spin up numerous fake identities on a single physical knoll, the prohibitive resource costs associated with the cryptographic verification render mass replication economically unviable.
